ja: 週末で一番楽しかったのは、実は久しぶりに家で何もしないでのんびりしたことなんだ。
en: What I enjoyed most about the weekend was actually relaxing at home and doing nothing for the first time in a while.
alternatives: The thing I enjoyed most about the weekend was actually relaxing at home and doing nothing for the first time in a while.
What I enjoyed most this weekend was actually just relaxing at home and doing nothing for the first time in ages.
point: 「一番〜なのは」は What I enjoyed most was で始める

ja: 先週末は雨がひどかったから、子どもたちには一日中家で好きなゲームをさせてあげたんだ。
en: The rain was so heavy last weekend that I let the kids play whatever games they wanted at home all day.
alternatives: It rained so hard last weekend that I let the kids play any games they liked at home all day.
Since it was pouring last weekend, I let my kids play whatever games they wanted at home all day long.
point: 「させてあげた」は let + 人 + 動詞の原形（to は不要）

ja: 新しい家の写真、見せてよ。
en: Show me some pictures of your new house.
alternatives: Show me some photos of your new place.
Show me a few pictures of your new house.
point: 複数の写真は pictures、漠然と「何枚か」なら some を付ける

ja: 雨がやんだら、私は歩いて駅まで行くよ。
en: I'll walk to the station when the rain stops.
alternatives: When the rain stops, I'll walk to the station.
I'll walk to the station once the rain stops.
point: 未来のことでも when 節は現在形 stops

ja: 天気予報では週末は雨だって言ってたのに、結局ずっと晴れてたね。
en: The forecast said it would rain this weekend, but it stayed sunny the whole time.
alternatives: The weather forecast said it was going to rain this weekend, but it was sunny the whole time.
They said it would rain this weekend, but it ended up being sunny all weekend.
point: said に合わせて will を would にする

ja: じゃあ、去年あの仕事を断ってなかったら、君は今ごろ大阪に住んでたかもしれないってこと？
en: So if you hadn't turned down that job last year, you might be living in Osaka now?
alternatives: So you might be living in Osaka now if you hadn't turned down that job last year?
So if you hadn't said no to that job last year, you could be living in Osaka now?
point: 去年の仮定は過去完了、今の状況は might be living

ja: 駅前のラーメン屋、いつも行列ができてるよね。行ったことある？
en: There's always a line at the ramen shop by the station. Have you tried it?
alternatives: There's always a long line at that ramen place near the station. Have you been there?
There's always a line outside the ramen shop by the station. Have you ever eaten there?
point: 「行列ができてる」は There's a line で言える

ja: 週末はどこに行ったの？
en: Where did you go this weekend?
alternatives: Where did you go on the weekend?
Where'd you go over the weekend?
point: 過去の疑問文は did + 動詞の原形

ja: 先週教えてもらったカフェ、行ってみたよ。すごくよかった。
en: I went to the café you told me about last week. It was great.
alternatives: I tried the café that you told me about last week, and I loved it.
I checked out the café you recommended last week. It was really good.
point: told me about の about を落とさない

ja: 天気予報をちゃんと見てたら、姉は土曜日のキャンプを延期してたと思うよ。
en: If my sister had checked the weather forecast, I think she would have postponed Saturday's camping trip.
alternatives: I think my sister would have put off Saturday's camping trip if she'd checked the forecast.
If my sister had looked at the weather forecast, she probably would have postponed her Saturday camping trip.
point: 過去の仮定は if + had 過去分詞、結果は would have

ja: 今夜は寒くなるよ。上着を持っていったほうがいいよ。
en: It'll be cold tonight. You should take a jacket.
alternatives: It's going to be cold tonight. You should bring a jacket.
It'll get cold tonight. You should take a coat.
point: 助言は should、have to だと強すぎる

ja: 昨日君が電話くれたとき、私は犬と遊んでいたんだ。
en: I was playing with my dog when you called yesterday.
alternatives: I was playing with the dog when you called yesterday.
When you called yesterday, I was playing with my dog.
point: 「〜していた」は過去進行形 was + -ing

ja: 今年の夏は去年よりずっと暑いですね。
en: This summer is much hotter than last year, isn't it?
alternatives: It's much hotter this summer than last year, isn't it?
This summer is a lot hotter than last year, isn't it?
point: 比較級を強めるのは very ではなく much や a lot

ja: 忙しかったけど、昔の友達に久しぶりに会えて、いい週末だったよ。
en: Although I was busy, I had a great weekend catching up with old friends.
alternatives: Even though I was busy, I had a great weekend catching up with old friends.
I was busy, but I had a nice weekend catching up with some old friends.
I was busy, but it was a good weekend because I got to see some old friends I hadn't seen in ages.
point: although の後に but は重ねない

ja: 引っ越してからもう半年だけど、新しい街にはもう慣れた？先月会ったときはまだ道に迷ってたよね。
en: It's been six months since you moved, so have you gotten used to the new town yet? You were still getting lost when I saw you last month.
alternatives: You moved six months ago, so are you used to the new town now? You were still getting lost when we met last month.
Have you settled into the new town yet? It's been six months since you moved, and you were still getting lost when I saw you last month.
point: 今の状態は現在完了、先月の様子は過去進行形で分ける

ja: すごく日焼けしてるね。先週の連休は、どこか暖かいところに行ってたに違いないね。
en: You're really tanned. You must have gone somewhere warm over last week's long weekend.
alternatives: You've got a great tan. You must have been somewhere warm over the long weekend last week.
You're so tanned. You must have gone somewhere warm for last week's long weekend.
point: 過去の推量「〜したに違いない」は must have + 過去分詞

ja: あのとき姉がキャンプに誘ってくれなかったら、私は今ごろこんなにアウトドアにハマってなかったと思う。
en: If my sister hadn't invited me camping back then, I don't think I'd be this into the outdoors now.
alternatives: I don't think I'd be so into the outdoors now if my sister hadn't invited me camping back then.
If my sister hadn't asked me to go camping back then, I don't think I'd be this into the outdoors now.
point: 過去の仮定は hadn't invited、今の結果は I'd be

ja: 今年の夏は暑かっただけでなく、雨もほとんど降らなかった。
en: Not only was this summer hot, but we also hardly had any rain.
alternatives: Not only was it hot this summer, but it also barely rained at all.
It wasn't just hot this summer; it also hardly rained at all.
point: Not only が文頭なら was this summer と語順が逆になる

ja: 今週末に僕が一番したいのは、家でゆっくりすることだよ。
en: What I want to do most this weekend is relax at home.
alternatives: What I most want to do this weekend is relax at home.
The thing I want to do most this weekend is relax at home.
point: 「〜したいこと」が主語。動詞は is で受ける

ja: 昨日の夜の花火大会、雨で中止になったんだって。
en: I heard last night's fireworks show was canceled because of the rain.
alternatives: I heard the fireworks last night got canceled because of the rain.
Apparently, last night's fireworks show was canceled due to the rain.
point: 「中止になった」は be/get canceled の受け身で

ja: 先週末に君が話してたカフェ、ついに行ってみたよ。もっと早く知っていればよかったなあ。
en: I finally tried that café you mentioned last weekend, and I wish I'd known about it much sooner.
alternatives: I finally went to the café you told me about last weekend, and I wish I'd found out about it sooner.
I finally checked out that café you mentioned last weekend. If only I'd known about it earlier!
point: 過去の後悔は I wish の後を過去完了 I'd known にする

ja: 駅前の新しいパン屋さんが何時に開くか知ってる？
en: Do you know what time the new bakery by the station opens?
alternatives: Do you know when the new bakery near the station opens?
Any idea what time the new bakery by the station opens?
point: 間接疑問は主語＋動詞の語順で does は使わない

ja: この前話した、隣に越してきたご夫婦が、先週末うちをバーベキューに誘ってくれたんだ。
en: The couple I told you about, the ones who moved in next door, invited us over for a barbecue last weekend.
alternatives: You know the couple who moved in next door that I mentioned? They invited us to a barbecue last weekend.
That couple who moved in next door, the ones I told you about, invited us to a barbecue last weekend.
point: 長い主語を関係節でまとめてから動詞 invited へ

ja: 週末の旅行の写真を私に送ってって、姉に頼んでおいたよ。
en: I asked my sister to send me the photos from our weekend trip.
alternatives: I've asked my sister to send me the pictures from our weekend trip.
I asked my sister to send me our weekend trip photos.
point: ask＋人＋to do の形で、人の後に to を置く

ja: 今日は本当に暑いですね。窓を開けてもいいですか？
en: It's really hot today. Is it okay if I open the window?
alternatives: It's really hot today. Do you mind if I open the window?
It's really hot today. May I open the window?
point: Is it okay if I の後は動詞の現在形
